nodes.label: Cloudflare Quick Tunnel
nodes.rationale: A free random https://….trycloudflare.com address that exists while cloudflared runs, so the assistant's servers can reach a Mac behind NAT with no Cloudflare account and no inbound port.

nodes.label: Loopback-Only Listener on Port 7419
nodes.rationale: House Control listens on the loopback interface only, so nothing on the local network sees it and the tunnel is the sole route in.

nodes.label: 128-Bit Key in Every Path
nodes.rationale: Every address carries a random 128-bit key; without it every path answers 404, so the public tunnel address alone is not enough to reach the home.

nodes.label: Action Links (/do/…)
nodes.rationale: Opening an action link performs the action and answers with the new state, so even an assistant that can only browse pages can run the home.

nodes.label: MCP Server over Streamable HTTP
nodes.rationale: Model Context Protocol at /<key>/mcp with JSON responses and no server-sent events, so Claude, ChatGPT and Claude Code can change the home itself, not only open links.

nodes.label: OpenAPI 3.1 Description
nodes.rationale: Exposes the same tools as plain HTTP + JSON for Custom GPT actions and agent frameworks, so using an assistant does not require MCP support.

nodes.label: edit_floor_plan Tool
nodes.rationale: A list of operations applied together, including furnish_room which replaces everything in a room, so a photo of a living room can become the room in 3D.

nodes.label: undo_floor_plan_edit Tool
nodes.rationale: Puts the plan back as it was before the last change, so an aggressive assistant edit is always reversible from the window or by the assistant itself.

nodes.label: render_home Tool
nodes.rationale: Returns a picture of the 3D model, whole or one room, so the assistant can check its own work.

nodes.label: What It May Do Permission Switches
nodes.rationale: Device control and 3D-home editing are separate switches that take effect immediately even while the link is live; turning devices off makes the link read-only.

nodes.label: Auto-Stop Timer
nodes.rationale: The link can stop itself after 1 hour, 8 hours (the default) or never, limiting how long a leaked address stays a house key.

nodes.label: Live Activity Feed
nodes.rationale: Everything an assistant reads or does shows up as it happens, with sparkles in the panel and island, so the user can watch the assistant work.

nodes.label: AI Access Privacy Model
nodes.rationale: The assistant's provider sees room and device names, their state and the floor plan, but never the Smart Life sign-in or real device IDs. Cloudflare relays the connection like any HTTPS proxy; 'This Mac only' avoids the tunnel entirely. Nothing is stored except the three settings and the link lives only in memory.

nodes.label: linked:true Device ID Redaction
nodes.rationale: Real device IDs are replaced by "linked": true, a plan the assistant writes keeps them as they were, and devices linked to hardware cannot be removed through the link.

nodes.label: Rate Limit and 4 MB Body Cap
nodes.rationale: Requests are limited to 240 a minute and bodies to 4 MB, bounding what a misbehaving or hostile client can do with a valid key.

nodes.label: This Mac Only Reach
nodes.rationale: Skips the tunnel and serves http://127.0.0.1:7419/<key>, for assistants running on the Mac such as Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, LM Studio and scripts.

nodes.label: cloudflared Developer ID Check
nodes.rationale: If cloudflared is missing the window offers to download it from Cloudflare's GitHub releases and keeps it only if it carries Cloudflare's Developer ID signature.

nodes.label: Plan Edit Validation
nodes.rationale: Edits are checked before saving: unknown furniture, overlapping ids and rooms that do not add up are refused with a reason the assistant can act on.
